tour.name: East Bali Private Tour: Lempuyang 'Gates of Heaven', Tirta Gangga & Besakih Mother Temple
tour.subtitle: A private day in Bali's quieter east with a licensed guide and car: the split gate of Pura Lempuyang framing Mount Agung, the water palace of Tirta Gangga and its stepping stones, lunch with a view of the rice terraces of Sidemen, and Besakih, the mother temple of Bali on the slopes of the holy mountain.

tour.overview:
The east of Bali is dominated by Mount Agung, 3,031 metres high, the island's highest volcano and the home of the gods in Balinese belief. On its slopes stand Besakih, the 'mother temple' of more than 80 temples in which all Balinese Hindus share, and Pura Lempuyang, one of the oldest temples on the island, whose split gate perfectly frames the mountain. Below, in the valleys, lie the water palaces built by the kings of Karangasem and terraced rice fields far from the crowds of the south.

This private day explores East Bali with a licensed guide and a car. You start early at Lempuyang to photograph the Gates of Heaven with fewer people, visit the water palace of Tirta Gangga, have lunch above the Sidemen valley and end at Besakih.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 12 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Bali
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; steps at Lempuyang and Besakih

WHAT YOU SEE
• Pura Lempuyang and its split gate.
• Tirta Gangga water palace.
• The Sidemen valley.
• Besakih mother temple.

WHY THIS WORKS
The queue for the famous photo at Lempuyang can exceed two hours by mid-morning; we arrive at dawn and then visit the rest of the east at a relaxed pace.

WHO IT SUITS
Photographers, culture lovers and anyone who wants to see Bali away from the crowds.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer a shorter day, choose our Ubud tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The 'mirror lake' reflection in the famous photos is made with a mirror held by a local photographer; your guide explains so you are not disappointed. Mount Agung is often in cloud after mid-morning. A sarong is required in all temples.

days.name: Pura Lempuyang at dawn, Tirta Gangga water palace, lunch above Sidemen and Besakih mother temple
days.description:
What to expect: the temples and landscapes of East Bali, with a licensed guide, private car, entrance fees and lunch.

Your driver and guide collect you at your hotel at about 4:00 and drive east in the dark, about two hours. At Pura Lempuyang, a shuttle takes you up the hill to the first temple, Penataran Agung, where the split gate, the candi bentar, frames Mount Agung like a window. Arriving at opening time means a short wait for the classic photograph, and, on clear mornings, the volcano glowing in the first light. Your guide explains the temple, one of the six sanctuaries of the world in Balinese belief, and the long climb of 1,700 steps to the highest shrine, which keen walkers can attempt.

You drive down to Tirta Gangga, 'water of the Ganges', a water palace built in 1946 by the last king of Karangasem. Its terraced gardens are filled with ponds of koi carp, fountains, statues of gods and demons, and octagonal stepping stones that let you walk across the water. Holy water from a spring feeds the pools, and locals still come to bathe in the swimming pool.

Lunch is at a restaurant above the Sidemen valley, where rice terraces step down to the river with Mount Agung behind. In the afternoon you visit Besakih, the mother temple, a complex of 23 temples climbing the mountainside in terraces, with black-roofed meru towers of up to eleven tiers. Your guide takes you through the main temple, Pura Penataran Agung, explains its importance to every Balinese family and its survival of the eruption of 1963, when the lava stopped just short of it. You are back at your hotel at about 16:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
04:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
06:00 – Pura Lempuyang at sunrise.
08:30 – Breakfast stop.
09:30 – Tirta Gangga water palace.
11:30 – Lunch above the Sidemen valley.
13:00 – Besakih mother temple.
14:30 – Drive back.
16:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Lempuyang's famous 'reflection' is created with a mirror under the phone; there is no lake.
• On ceremony days, parts of Besakih may be closed to visitors, but the festivities are wonderful to see.
• Avoid unofficial guides at Besakih; your licensed guide accompanies you throughout.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, entrance fees and shuttle, sarongs, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: breakfast, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Why such an early start?
faq.answer: To reach Lempuyang at opening, before the long queues for the famous photo and while Mount Agung is most often clear.

faq.question: Is the 'lake' in the photos real?
faq.answer: No. Photographers at the gate hold a mirror under the phone to create the reflection. It is still a beautiful view.

faq.question: Are the entrance fees included?
faq.answer: Yes: Lempuyang with the shuttle, Tirta Gangga and Besakih, plus sarongs.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, above the Sidemen valley. Vegetarian and other diets are easy to arrange.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, for children who don't mind an early start. They love the stepping stones and fish at Tirta Gangga. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The first gate at Lempuyang is reached by shuttle and steps; Besakih is a steep complex. Tirta Gangga is easier.

faq.question: What is the dress code?
faq.answer: A sarong and sash in all temples (provided), and shoulders covered.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Bali but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes, a light jacket for the early morning, and clothes covering shoulders.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to October, when Mount Agung is most often visible. In the rainy season, mornings are still the clearest.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
